mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Company Registration (Certificate of Incorporation) of the Korean Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry Office of the Local District Court under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A (Hague Apostille member state): Court-certified extract from the District Court Registry -> Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) Apostille Division. Route B (Non-member state): Court-certified extract -> MOFA consular affairs legalization -> Embassy/Consulate of the destination state in Korea. Route A and Route B are parallel alternatives and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Current Registration Extract showing no liquidation, rehabilitation, or dissolution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local District Court Registry Office having jurisdiction over the company's registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A (Apostille Convention state): Registry-issued current extract -> MOFA Apostille. Route B (Non-member state): Registry-issued current extract -> MOFA legalization -> destination-state Embassy/Consulate in Korea. Use only the route applicable to the receiving jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing officers, foreign counsel, and the agent for process and apostille/legalization filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Korean Chusik Hoesa, authenticated by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A (Apostille Convention state): Directors' signatures notarized by Korean notary -> MOFA Apostille. Route B (Non-member state): Notarized resolution -> MOFA consular legalization -> destination-state Embassy/Consulate in Korea. The routes are alternative; never present both as one chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Articles of Association (registered copy of the company's statutes, including business purpose of international media relations and crisis public relations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry Office after registration; company secretary for the pre-registration draft
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A (Apostille Convention state): Certified copy of registered Articles -> MOFA Apostille. Route B (Non-member state): Certified copy -> MOFA legalization -> destination-state Embassy/Consulate in Korea. Mutually exclusive routes only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the designated Korean bank in the name of the new Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding Korean bank (e.g., Hana Bank, Woori Bank, Shinhan Bank, or KB Kookmin Bank) through the relationship banking team
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A (Apostille Convention state): Bank officer signature/company seal authenticated by Korean notary -> MOFA Apostille. Route B (Non-member state): Bank-sealed letter notarized -> MOFA consular legalization -> destination-state Embassy/Consulate in Korea. The two authentication pathways are exclusive and never cumulative.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding any shareholder, director, officer, ultimate beneficial owner, client, or contractual counterparty, the Korean Chusik Hoesa must screen against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Consolidated Sanctions Lists, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Sanctions List, the KoFIU watchlists, and the FATF and APG public statements. Enhanced PEP due diligence must include source-of-wealth/source-of-funds evidence, independent media searches, senior-management approval for any high-risk relationship, and continuous transaction monitoring for ACH and wire payment rails. Screening results must be preserved for seven years after account closure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) Corporate Name Search and Registration System, accessible at www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be registered in Korean (Hangeul) and must include the Korean designation corresponding to Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation). A foreign-language or romanized name may be added only as an auxiliary registered trade name and must not be identical or deceptively similar to any existing registered corporate name. The clearance hierarchy follows four tiers: exact Korean spelling, Korean transliteration of a foreign name, romanized transliteration, and auxiliary English trade name. Authorities also require the business-purpose clause to be consistent with the registered name and the ISIC 7310 / overseas PR communications scope.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 calendar days of receiving a formal name rejection from the Registry Office, the applicant, through its authorized representative, must submit a written objection to the Registry department of the District Court and a simultaneous Request for Reconsideration to the Supreme Court Registry Office under the Commercial Registration Rules. The appeal must provide a comparative list of similar registered names, explain the distinctive and non-deceptive character of the proposed name, attach the company's draft Articles of Association and business-purpose certificate, and pay the applicable appeal court fee. If the Registry does not issue a favorable decision within 30 days, the applicant may appeal to the Seoul Administrative Court for judicial revocation of the rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in South Korea must be a fixed, identifiable address in the Articles of Association and must be accepted by the District Court Registry as the company's head office. A virtual office or commercial mailbox is technically permissible for court registration if supplied by a licensed corporate-services provider with a dedicated office unit, signboard, mail-handling protocol, and visitor reception, but the National Tax Service and Korean banks for an ISIC 7310 overseas PR communications firm will likely reject a pure virtual mailbox without a physical lease. In practice, for retainers paid by ACH and wire, banks require a real floor desk, utility bill, and on-site representative before opening corporate accounts. Therefore, virtual office is permissibility only under a full executive-suite arrangement with physical presence during business hours and no letterhead-only address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 15-25% likelihood of an unannounced National Tax Service business-site confirmation visit within the first 12 months for a low-risk PR firm; if the registered address is a virtual office, the risk rises to approximately 40% due to paper-company flags. Checklist: (1) company nameplate or signboard visible at the registered address; (2) valid lease agreement and electricity/utility invoice matching the address; (3) employee or officer present during business hours; (4) books, records, computers, and client deliverables available for review; (5) mail receipt and forwarding log; (6) board meeting minutes and share register stored at the address; (7) if independently managed office, registered sublease and authorized-mail agreements in place.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: The Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended; in particular Articles 288, 289, 295, 302, 316, 317, 329, 330, 363, 368, 382, 389, and 393; the Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Act; and the Supreme Court Regulation on Registration of Commercial Matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the company's registered office, including the Seoul Central District Court for Seoul-based companies, and the online I-REG corporate registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Chusik Hoesa) under Article 317 of the Commercial Act, together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation; completion is evidenced by a Certificate of Registered Matters (corporate registry extract).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa. The aggregate share subscription price must be paid into a bank capital subscription account in the name of the company before the incorporation registration is filed, and the funds must remain in that account until registration is completed. No blocked escrow account is required for this non-licensable service corporation. Registration license tax and court fees are payable separately based on the stated capital and filing schedule.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, effective as of the date of this meeting, that the following actions be and they hereby are authorized, ratified, confirmed, and directed: 1. Capital Subscription and Allotment. The subscriptions set forth in the share subscription report are accepted, and all issued shares are allotted to the subscribers named in the share subscription report. The directors shall verify that each subscriber has paid the full subscription amount to the capital subscription account established in the name of the Company. The directors are authorized to execute share certificates and deliver them to shareholders upon registration. 2. Banking Authorization. The Representative Director is authorized and directed to open and maintain corporate operating, foreign currency, and settlement accounts at a commercial bank selected by management; to designate signatories and electronic banking administrators; and to negotiate direct-debit retainer collection through ACH and wire facilities. Any two directors or the Representative Director together with the Chief Financial Officer shall approve transactions above USD 50,000 or the Korean Won equivalent. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office of the Company shall be the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation. The Representative Director is directed to file the registered office notice with the district court, record the office with the National Tax Service and local municipal tax office, and post the required notice at the registered address. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The following persons are appointed as first officers of the Company to serve until the first ordinary general meeting of shareholders and until successors are duly elected or appointed: [Name] as Representative Director; [Name] as Director; and [Name] as Statutory Auditor. The Statutory Auditor shall have the inspection and reporting rights granted by the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea. 5. Board Governance. The Board adopts the Corporate Governance and Board Operations Rules. The Board may establish committees, delegate management powers as permitted by Article 393, and call extraordinary meetings when necessary. The directors shall exercise due care and loyalty under Article 382. 6. Professional Advisers and Formation Logistics. The Representative Director is authorized to retain legal counsel, certified public accountants, tax agents, and other advisers; to execute all applications and instruments; to pay registration fees and taxes; to apply for the business registration certificate; and to complete bank account setup and all registrations with the tax and labor authorities. 7. Ratification and Effectiveness. All acts taken by the incorporators, directors, or officers in connection with the formation and incorporation of the Company before the date of this resolution are hereby ratified and confirmed. These resolutions are effective immediately and shall continue until revoked or amended. The Corporate Secretary is directed to record these resolutions in the corporate minute book and to deliver certified copies to the appointed officers and lending banks.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Search and Articles of Incorporation Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Information System (I-REG) and Commercial Registration Division of the District Court with jurisdiction over the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search on the I-REG online registry to verify that the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered corporate name in the Republic of Korea. Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in compliance with the Commercial Act, specifying the corporate name, objectives, registered address, authorized share capital, par value per share, classes of shares, method of incorporation, number of directors and auditors, fiscal year end, public notice method, and the place where notices are published. Every incorporator must sign or affix his or her seal to the articles, and the articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public before filing. If an English trade name is to be used in addition to the Korean name, include it in the articles and provide supporting evidence of the transliteration. This step is completed before any registration fee is paid and before capital subscription.
required_dossiers: Incorporators' identification documents and sealed powers of attorney
Seal impression certificate and personal seal
Proposed registered office address and lease agreement draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or I-REG indicates a conflict, amend the proposed name by adding a distinguishing element or choose a new name and repeat the search; no judicial appeal is necessary before filing, but a formal name objection can be raised with the court only after registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles and Opening of Capital Subscription Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public in the district of the company's registered office and the designated commercial bank branch opening the capital subscription account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the incorporators approve the final articles, each incorporator must appear before a notary public, declare their intention to incorporate the Chusik Hoesa, and sign or seal the articles in the notary's presence. The notary will certify a copy of the articles and return the original for registration. Simultaneously, the incorporators must open a temporary capital subscription account in the name of the company to be incorporated with a Korean commercial bank. The full subscription amount for the shares being issued must be transferred into this account. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit or balance confirmation identifying the depositor, the intended corporate name, and the amount paid. This certificate is a mandatory attachment to the registration application. Any in-kind contributions must be appraised by an appraiser and described in the articles.
required_dossiers: Written consent of each subscribing director and auditor
Copies of identification of all incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests source-of-funds documentation, provide bank statements, gift declarations, or loan agreements; if notarization lacks a required seal, return to the notary to re-execute. The deposit certificate should be reissued if the corporate name changes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Registration with the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court or the local District Court Branch exercising jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for registration of incorporation to the Commercial Registration Division in person or through an agent. The application must be in the prescribed court form and accompanied by the notarized articles, the capital subscription deposit certificate, consents of directors and the auditor, and evidence of the registered office. Pay the registration license tax, local education tax, and court filing fee using the court's prescribed payment procedure. The registration officer will review the application for statutory defects. Upon acceptance, the court assigns a corporate registration number and records the company. The registrar will issue a certificate of registered matters, commonly called a corporate registry extract, that evidences the legal existence of the company. The company comes into existence on the date of this registration rather than on the date the articles are signed.
required_dossiers: Certificate of capital subscription deposit from bank
Consents to appointment of directors and auditor
Certificate of personal seal impression of the representative director
Registered office lease agreement or title certificate
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
Proof of payment of registration license tax and court fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order or suspension notice, cure the identified defect within the stated period by filing a supplementary document or correcting the application; if the period lapses, submit a fresh application with a new payment. An objection or administrative appeal can be filed with the court or the National Court Administration as appropriate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with mandatory electronic filing through the HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr). The Korean tax administration is centralized and unitary; the competent district tax office is determined by the corporation's registered head office address. Customs matters are administered by the Korea Customs Service (UNI-PASS) where goods are exported.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa incorporated under the Korean Commercial Act is a domestic corporation and must register with the NTS by filing a business registration application (corporation type) with the district tax office within 20 days from commencement of business and in any event no later than the corporate tax registration deadline of 3 months from incorporation. The issued 10-digit Business Registration Number serves simultaneously as the corporate TIN, VAT registration number, and withholding agent account number. The registration may be completed online via HomeTax using the legal representative's authentication certificate; if the foreign legal representative has no resident registration number, a joint security certificate is required through the relevant tax office, and a domestic tax representative must be appointed for service of process and tax payment administration. The full procedure includes: (1) filing the articles of incorporation and certificate of incorporation; (2) submitting the lease contract and business-premises evidence; (3) obtaining the 10-digit Business Registration Number; (4) completing local tax registration with the competent local government for local income tax (residence tax) surcharge; and (5) opening a foreign currency account with a Korean foreign exchange bank and filing the related foreign exchange declaration for export receivables.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope: A Chusik Hoesa is the Korean statutory stock corporation and is by default an independent corporate taxpayer under the Corporate Income Tax Act. As a domestic corporation, it is taxed on worldwide income, while non-resident and foreign corporate shareholders are taxed only on Korean-source income. No pass-through or transparency treatment is available. Local income tax (residence tax) is imposed as a 10 percent surcharge on corporate income tax. Dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are subject to Korean withholding tax at the statutory 22 percent aggregate rate (20 percent corporate plus 2 percent local), subject to treaty reduction. The entity is also liable as a withholding agent for payroll and cross-border payments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Korean tax law does not contain a US-style check-the-box election. The available statutory elections relevant to this structure are: (1) consolidated corporate income tax return election for a wholly-owned domestic corporate group under Article 76-2 of the Corporate Income Tax Act, requiring application to the NTS and applying to all qualifying group members; (2) the VAT zero-rating and foreign-currency-settlement election under Article 21(1)(e) of the VAT Act for cross-border service supplies, exercised through issuance of zero-rated e-tax invoices in the prescribed form; (3) the foreign tax credit versus foreign tax deduction election under Article 57(2) of the Corporate Income Tax Act for overseas branch and foreign-source income; and (4) hybrid mismatch rules under OECD BEPS Action 2, which apply compulsorily and are not elective; Korea maintains no hybrid entity classification election for Chusik Hoesa.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea; a credit-invoice European-style VAT on supplies of goods and services with quarterly filing and mandatory e-invoice reporting.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no de minimis VAT turnover threshold above which registration is required in Korea; registration is mandatory for any business operator, including a Chusik Hoesa, that makes taxable supplies. A simplified taxation regime for individuals applies below KRW 80,000,000 annual turnover, but juridical persons such as Chusik Hoesa are categorically excluded from simplified taxation and must always file standard quarterly VAT returns irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea mandates fully electronic tax invoices (e-Tax Invoices) for all VAT-registered corporations. Every taxable supply, including zero-rated exports, must be evidenced by an e-Tax Invoice transmitted to the NTS HomeTax e-invoicing system no later than the day following the supply date. The NTS performs real-time clearance by issuing a unique management (acceptance) number to each e-invoice; AP/ERP integration is required and supported by the NTS Open API for e-invoice and returns, which issues acknowledgment receipts. No paper invoice option exists for B2B and B2G supplies; no separate digital stamping tax applies, as the statutory electronic invoice is validated through the centralized NTS database. Failure to transmit e-invoices attracts an additional tax of 2 percent of the supply value, and delayed issuance attracts an additional tax of 1 percent.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating at 0 percent VAT is available for exported goods under Article 21(1)(1) of the VAT Act and for services supplied to non-residents that are actually consumed or utilized outside Korea, in particular advertising, public relations, communication services, and other offshore business services qualifying under Article 21(1)(e) of the VAT Act and Article 26(1)(7) of its Enforcement Decree. For this ISIC 7310 global PR agency, the eligibility conditions are: the service is rendered exclusively to a customer without a domestic place of business in Korea; the service is for use in promoting the customer's business outside Korea; payment is denominated in foreign currency and collected from outside Korea; and the entity retains an executed offshore engagement contract plus an inbound foreign-exchange receipt certificate. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated supplies is fully creditable and refundable. Pure offshore PR retainers qualify, but domestic media buying and domestic campaign management do not; mixed contracts must be split into taxable domestic and zero-rated offshore portions with separate e-invoices.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Zero-rated electronic tax invoice transmitted via NTS HomeTax with the zero-rating code for the transaction
Executed international PR service agreement or media placement contract identifying the non-resident customer, offshore market, and service scope
Certificate of receipt of foreign exchange (inward remittance or foreign exchange purchase certificate from a Korean foreign exchange bank) evidencing settlement of the export consideration
Customs Export Declaration (UNI-PASS electronic declaration) for any physical or tangible export component, such as marketing media assets, branded merchandise, or printed collateral
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for tangible goods movement accompanying the service export, if applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS treats false export zero-rating and artificial offshore billing as aggravated tax evasion. The consequences are: (1) retroactive reassessment clawing back the 10 percent VAT previously zero-rated, plus an additional tax of 40 percent of the underpaid amount for deceitful non-filing or under-reporting under Article 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes; (2) denial of input VAT credits traced to fictitious export transactions; (3) penalty interest at the statutory overdue rate; (4) criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act with imprisonment of up to 2 years or a fine of up to 2 times the tax evaded; and (5) corporate blacklisting for intensive NTS audit selection, which may trigger an integrated customs and foreign-exchange probe with secondary penalties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for failure to collect export proceeds within 180 days unless a prescribed extension is approved.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as co-administrators of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA); operational enforcement and declaration processing are delegated to authorized foreign exchange banks, and transaction-level surveillance is centralized in the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). The Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KFIU) supervise bank conduct and AML/CFT obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Current-account transactions, including overseas PR retainer receipts, subcontract payments, media placement disbursements, and licensing fees, are fully liberalized and require no prior MOEF approval; they must be routed through an authorized foreign exchange bank with a Foreign Exchange Declaration form and underlying contract or invoice, and the resulting data is captured in FEIS. Capital-account transactions remain restricted or reporting-based: inward foreign direct investment (FDI) must be filed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) with MOEF, KOTRA, or a delegated authorized bank; foreign borrowings above prescribed thresholds require MOEF/BOK reporting; and outward investment requires prior filing. The Korean won (KRW) is not an internationally convertible currency; non-residents may not freely hold onshore KRW accounts without a permitted purpose, and offshore KRW liquidity is confined to the licensed NDF market. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is lawful but subject to sequential hurdles: (i) confirmation of distributable reserves via audited financial statements; (ii) a shareholder dividend resolution and board resolution; (iii) withholding of the 22% dividend tax (20% plus 10% local surtax) or a treaty-reduced rate evidenced by a tax clearance certificate or National Tax Service confirmation; (iv) proof of FIPA-registered shareholding matching the remittee; and (v) completion of the FX declaration and FEIS reporting by the remitting bank. The bank may also request a foreign-invested company registration certificate and an overseas remittance report before executing the wire.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The Republic of Korea abolished mandatory surrender of export proceeds in 1998. Proceeds earned from overseas PR services (invisible trade or current-account receipts) must be repatriated to an authorized foreign exchange bank within the permitted settlement term, generally one year from the invoice date or completion of service, with documented extension available for justified commercial delay. The Chusik Hoesa is not required to convert foreign currency into KRW; proceeds may be retained indefinitely in a Foreign Currency Deposit (FCD) account, converted at market rates, or used directly for permitted current-account payments. All receipts above the de minimis threshold (USD 5,000 or KRW equivalent) must be declared via the FX Declaration form, and the bank will record the receipt in FEIS. Failure to settle or repatriate within the statutory period without approval exposes the company to administrative fines under FETA.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FIPA Capital Escrow Account, KRW Operational Account, and Foreign Currency Deposit (FCD) Account
KRW Operational Account and Foreign Currency Deposit (FCD) Account
KRW Operational Account and Foreign Currency Deposit (FCD) Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW feasibility and legally constrained. Foreign electronic money institutions licensed under UK FCA EMI, EU EMI, or US money transmitter regimes are not recognized as authorized foreign exchange banks under FETA and cannot hold onshore KRW transactional accounts, cannot execute statutory FX declarations, and cannot file FEIS reports for a Korean resident entity. The Chusik Hoesa must maintain its primary treasury, FX, and settlement accounts with a domestic authorized foreign exchange bank. An offshore EMI may serve only as an auxiliary collection or disbursement wallet for non-KRW payments (e.g., USD or EUR client retainers), provided balances are swept daily into the Korean FCD account; using an EMI as the principal clearing rail creates regulatory, tax reporting, and audit deficiencies and risks fines for non-declared foreign receipts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PHYSICAL ATTENDANCE IS REQUIRED for first-time foreign directors and signatories without an Alien Registration Card (ARC). Major Korean banks uniformly require at least one joint representative director to appear in person at a corporate banking centre with an original passport, valid entry visa, apostilled certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, corporate seal certificate, and board resolution authorizing account opening. Remote or video-call onboarding is available only in narrow cases where the signatory is a Korean-resident director holding an ARC and the bank's compliance team approves a live interview; even then, courier delivery of wet-ink documents is mandatory. Given the Low_Risk_Standard AML profile of an international PR agency, banks will accept the account, but the foreign-director physical interview remains the enforceable precondition for activating online banking and wire capabilities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity with nominee or multi-tier offshore shareholder layers above the Chusik Hoesa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized UBO declaration listing all natural-person owners holding 25% or more and the full control chain; corporate registry extracts and shareholder ledger; apostilled articles of incorporation; certificate of corporate seal; bank-specific UBO questionnaire; organizational chart tracing each intermediate entity to the ultimate individual; negative media and sanctions screening report for every named person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign director without ARC, without verifiable Korean residential address, and unable to present an in-person interview
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original passport with valid visa; proof of overseas residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within three months); apostilled certificate of incorporation and certificate of incumbency from the home jurisdiction; board resolution appointing the director and specifying account signatories; scheduled physical branch appointment with the Relationship Manager and Compliance Officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection sourced from a jurisdiction on FATF grey-list, a non-treaty jurisdiction, or a jurisdiction with sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds narrative letter with sworn undertaking; six-month bank statements of the investing shareholder; commercial contract or business plan evidencing the genuine funding need; tax residence certificate of the investor; sanctions and negative news screening report; corporate register extract confirming the investor's legitimacy; breakdown of the funding into debt and equity components.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual outbound transaction velocity or high-value wires inconsistent with the PR-service billing cycle, particularly to media vendors or subcontractors in offshore territories
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed service-level agreements with overseas clients; itemized invoices and payment schedules; deliverable evidence such as media placement reports and campaign analytics; subcontractor agreements and vendor due diligence files; tax invoices; quarterly VAT returns and corporate tax payments evidencing consistency between invoiced revenue, bank receipts, and declared income.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or politically connected counterparty appearing on the client or vendor roster
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence questionnaire completed by the counterparty; source-of-wealth declaration for the PEP; board-approved AML/CFT policy and client acceptance procedure; documented commercial rationale for the engagement; consent to ongoing transaction monitoring; independent legal opinion where the PEP relationship involves government procurement or state-affiliated media.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital must arrive by SWIFT MT103 from the FIPA-registered foreign investor to the Chusik Hoesa account at an authorized foreign exchange bank. The remitter's legal name, account number, and jurisdiction must exactly match the investor recorded on the FIPA Foreign Investment Report; mismatches cause automatic compliance holds. Upon receipt, the bank credits the Foreign Currency Deposit or KRW capital account, issues a Foreign Currency Deposit Receipt and Purchase/Sales Record, and files the FEIS declaration. The FIPA report must be lodged with MOEF, KOTRA, or the delegated bank before or promptly after the capital contribution, and the company must complete the foreign-invested company registration to unlock full repatriation rights. The remittance purpose code must reflect equity participation (the MOEF capital-transaction classification for FDI rather than a current-account service code). The supporting verification dossier comprises: the FIPA report form and registration certificate, board resolution and shareholder resolution authorizing the share issuance, share subscription agreement, amended articles of incorporation reflecting the capital increase, certificate of corporate seal, and signatory identification. Where capital enters as a shareholder loan rather than equity, the borrowing must be reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations and a separate loan agreement plus drawn-down schedule must be retained.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails are: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct cross-border wires to overseas clients, media vendors, and subcontractors, with current-account service purpose codes and the underlying invoice or contract retained for FEIS validation; (2) SWIFT MT202 COV for cover payments where the beneficiary bank operates through a correspondent in a different currency zone; (3) commercial documentary letters of credit (sight and usance) for procurement of production services, media inventory, or event logistics where the beneficiary requires LC security; and (4) domestic disbursements in Korean won via the KFTC HOFINET wire network for ordinary vendor payments and BOK-WIRE+ RTGS for high-value same-day settlements. Every outbound wire requires a Foreign Exchange Declaration, supporting commercial documents, and tax verification where the payment constitutes a deductible expense; the bank maps each payment to an R-series service purpose code and screens the beneficiary against sanctions and watchlists. For recurring retainer-based outflows, the company should establish a standing settlement instruction file with the Relationship Manager to expedite dual-control release and reduce per-transaction friction. The treasury should maintain compensating won balances and a USD FCD buffer to avoid failed-settlement charges and to execute vendor payments without forced spot conversion.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW/USD and KRW/EUR foreign exchange forward contracts on a real-demand basis, with tenors aligned to the underlying PR retainer receivables and subcontractor payables.
FX swaps and rollover extensions transacted with the authorized foreign exchange bank to bridge mismatches between retainer receipt dates and disbursement dates.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts for KRW executed through the onshore licensed bank or a global treasury desk, permitted strictly where the company can document real trade exposure and the contract is for hedging rather than speculation.
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) hedging long-term foreign-currency liabilities, including shareholder loans or multi-year overseas media commitments.

Plain-vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars (forward-plus-option structures) with real-demand documentation, subject to the bank's product eligibility review and the company's board-approved hedging policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Shareholders (Art. 365 Korean Commercial Act) and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the company; minutes filed with the registry upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year; fiscal year-end commonly December 31, so by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government fine for delayed AGM, but failure to approve financial statements may invalidate audit exemption and trigger external inspection; persistent violation may lead to administrative penalties and forced dissolution by court order

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual tax return and corporate income tax filing under the Corporate Income Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax system (Hometax.go.kr)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20% of unpaid tax; failure to pay triggers an additional 0.022% daily interest charge (approximately 8.03% annualized); continued delinquency can lead to collection procedures and administrative seizure of assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax surtax return (Resident Tax) on the corporate income tax liability
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of the registered business address (e.g., Seoul Metropolitan Government)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the corporate income tax return; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional 10% non-filing penalty on the unpaid local income tax; daily late payment interest accrues; enforced collection through local tax authorities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax (VAT) interim and final returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Semi-annual filing: first half (January–June) due by July 25; second half (July–December) due by January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% non-filing or underreporting penalty; daily late payment interest of 0.022%; possible criminal prosecution for intentional evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Withholding tax on salaries of directors and employees and on foreign vendor payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly filing by the 10th of the following month; semiannual simplified filing available for small employers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% negligence penalty on unreported withheld amounts; administrative penalties; criminal liability for deliberate failure to withhold

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial registration annual update report under Commercial Registry Act (report on changes, not an annual renewal filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: District Court Registrar (Registration Office) having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual due date; filing required within 14 days after any change in directors, officers, registered office, or capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Imposition of a nominal administrative fine up to KRW 1,000,000 (approx. USD 750); repeated non-compliance can lead to compulsory fine under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership and Major Shareholder Reporting under the Act on the Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), an affiliate of the Bank of Korea; data filed through the Financial Supervisory Service's system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of the fiscal year if there have been changes in beneficial ownership; otherwise no annual filing is required except upon establishment or registration changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of up to KRW 30,000,000 (approx. USD 22,500) for failure to report; criminal penalties of imprisonment up to 3 years or fines for willful violation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report filing under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the electronic disclosure system DART
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year-end; statutory auditor's report must be filed by March 31 for a December 31 year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 30,000,000 (approx. USD 22,500); possible criminal fine for non-compliance; audit report delay leads to denial of tax deduction for audit fees and may trigger forced correction orders

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employment Insurance, National Pension, Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance, and National Health Insurance premium payment and declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local social insurance authorities under the Ministry of Employment and Labor and National Health Insurance Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly premium payment by the 10th of the following month; annual wage declaration for social insurance adjustment due by March 15 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional 5% penalty per overdue month up to a maximum of 50% of unpaid premiums; enforced collection from bank accounts or other assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Contribution filing under the National Tax Collection Act for the enterprise benefits to employees (fringe-benefit fund tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual report by March 31 of the following year for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% negligence penalty on any unpaid tax; daily late payment interest at 0.022%; criminal prosecution for intentional underreporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Real estate holding tax return (comprehensive real estate holding tax) if the company owns real estate above the threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (province or metropolitan city) and NTS for comprehensive real estate holding tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Property tax: June 1 and December 1 for respective installments; comprehensive real estate holding tax: December 1 for annual filing and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax for non-filing; additional daily late payment interest of 0.022%; possible auction for prolonged non-payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Trade statistics report and foreign exchange transaction report, if the PR firm conducts overseas remittances above USD 5,000 (including contract fee remittances)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Customs Korea (statistics report) and Foreign Exchange Bank (contract and settlement report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Trade statistics report within the month following the transaction; foreign exchange report at the time of remittance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 20,000,000 (approx. USD 15,000) under the Act on Aggravated Punishment for Specific Economic Crimes; possible restriction of foreign exchange transactions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: External audit is mandatory for any Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) with two of the following three criteria at fiscal year-end: total assets of KRW 12,000,000,000 (approx. USD 9,000,000) or more, revenue of KRW 10,000,000,000 (approx. USD 7,500,000) or more, or 300 or more employees. Also, any corporation listed on the stock exchange or operating in a registered securities-related business must undergo a statutory audit irrespective of size. Additionally, if the company is required to file annual financial statements under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, an independent certified public accountant's audit is mandatory
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed entities and for unlisted entities above a certain scale; for smaller unlisted corporations, Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) as approved by the Financial Supervisory Commission are acceptable. For tax reporting, the Corporate Tax Act applies its own adjustments to the financial accounting basis

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information, each corporation must continuously maintain a register of real beneficial owners. Any transfer of shares resulting in a change of beneficial ownership must be reported to KoFIU within 30 days of the change. There is no separate annual beneficial ownership confirmation filing requirement under Korean law for a non-financial corporation; compliance is event-driven. However, the recent Amendment to the Commercial Act imposes a duty on the board of directors to identify and document the ultimate beneficial owner during the annual audit of the shareholder register, and the result must be reflected in the minutes of the annual general meeting. Under the Commercial Act, a non-listed stock corporation must maintain a complete register of members that identifies each shareholder and their respective shareholdings, and the register must be made available for inspection at the registered office. An annual confirmation of the register is not separately required by law but is prudent practice
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (records of shareholder and board meetings)
Register of Charges over Assets (if any)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,200 per annum depending on the chosen registered agent and office location (Seoul premium vs. Gyeonggi-do cost-effective)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 20,000 for a typical non-listed Chusik Hoesa within the ISIC 7310 advertising and public relations sector, subject to audit thresholds and complexity of cross-border transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; lower brackets apply at 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% above KRW 200 million, and 21% above KRW 20 billion. A 10% Local Income Tax surcharge on the national corporate income tax produces an aggregate top marginal rate of 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket statutory tax holiday exists for ISIC 7310 overseas public relations agencies. Qualifying foreign-invested enterprises may obtain reductions under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; R&D credit deductions and SME preferential brackets are available only when statutory eligibility is met. Routine PR retainer income does not qualify for a material effective-rate carve-out.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Amount Return, filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal; required supplementary schedules cover balance sheet, income statement, tax adjustments, international transactions, and foreign tax credit computations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. A corporation with prior-year national tax liability exceeding KRW 5 million must also make interim estimated prepayments on July 31 and November 30, with the annual return acting as the final reconciliation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final corporate income tax return must be filed within three months after the fiscal year-end; a calendar-year corporation files by March 31 of the following year. A foreign corporation with a Korean permanent establishment follows the same rule. A foreign corporation without a Korean permanent establishment is generally subject to source withholding and does not file a self-assessment return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing attracts an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid corporate tax. Underreporting attracts an additional 10% of the underreported amount. Daily overdue charges accrue at 0.022% per day, approximately 8.03% per annum, until the entire liability is paid. Failing to present mandated schedules can trigger separate negligence penalties up to KRW 10 million.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate Identification and Jurisdiction Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Korean Business Registration Number or the NTS-issued registration identifier for a foreign corporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean permanent establishment identification or obtain a non-resident corporate registration through a Korean tax representative before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of the fiscal year-end and reconciliation to the accounting period of the Korean establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean permanent establishment must generally align its fiscal year with the foreign head office unless the NTS has approved a different period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Gross Revenue and Business Profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue attributable to the Korean business, including overseas public relations service fees, retainer payments, and crisis-communication management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Korean-source and permanent-establishment-attributable revenue; overseas media outreach services performed and managed from Korea are generally sourced to Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Tax Adjustments and Taxable Base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of book income to taxable income after add-backs and deduction adjustments, including entertainment expense disallowances, non-deductible provisions, and excess contribution limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border head-office cost allocations are deductible only if contemporaneously supported as arm's length and economically connected to Korean operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Tax Credits and Treaty Relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit claims, research and development credits, unabsorbed losses, and non-resident treaty withholding relief computations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the NTS international transaction schedules, foreign tax vouchers, and the Tax Residency Certificate when claiming relief under any double tax agreement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Non-resident shareholders receiving dividends from a Korean Chusik Hoesa are subject to aggregate statutory withholding of 22%, comprising 20% national Corporate Income Tax withholding plus 2 percentage points representing the 10% Local Income Tax surcharge on the national withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Korean payer must withhold at the statutory rate and issue a non-resident withholding certificate. To obtain treaty relief, the non-resident recipient must file an application for treaty-convention withholding reduction or exemption with the competent District Tax Office, submitting the original Tax Residency Certificate issued by the residence-state tax authority, evidence of beneficial ownership, shareholding records, and a declaration of business purpose. Approval must generally be secured before the dividend distribution; if denied, a refund claim may be pursued within the three-year statutory correction period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 22% aggregate (20% national plus 2% local surcharge). Under Korea's tax treaties, rates are commonly reduced, for example: Korea-United States DTA interest 10% and royalties 15%; Korea-China DTA interest 10% and royalties 10%; Korea-Japan DTA interest 10% and royalties 10%. All treaty relief requires beneficial ownership and satisfaction of limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File submission is triggered when annual cross-border transactions with foreign related parties exceed KRW 5 billion. Master File and Country-by-Country Report obligations trigger when the multinational group's consolidated revenue for the preceding fiscal year exceeds KRW 100 billion. Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation should still be prepared for smaller cross-border related-party transactions involving an overseas PR agency.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not administer a standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to offshore financial centers. However, the Korean Framework Act on National Taxes contains a statutory substance-over-form principle, and the International Tax Adjustment Act includes general anti-abuse and anti-treaty-shopping rules. A Korean Chusik Hoesa or its overseas PR affiliate must demonstrate actual offices, personnel, management control, risk-taking, and operational activity; artificial arrangements designed to shift Korean-source retainer income to tax-favored jurisdictions will be recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of Korean-source public relations fees, falsification of books and invoices, creation of fictitious expenses through overseas shell vendors, or concealment of retainer revenue attributed to the Korean permanent establishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment for up to three years or a fine up to five times the evaded national tax under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, plus payment of the evaded tax, late-payment interest, and negligence penalties; administrative exclusion from government procurement and public subsidies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A controlling director, actual business operator, or de facto manager who caused the false filing may be criminally prosecuted and personally subjected to fines or imprisonment; the NTS can pierce the corporate entity where it is a sham, and unpaid corporate taxes may be collected from the individual's personal assets; departure bans are possible for delinquent tax amounts above KRW 50 million.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Artificial Foreign Affiliate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a Korean or offshore PR subsidiary without office premises, employees, bank accounts, business records, or decision-making functions; routing retainer fees through the shell to strip margin from Korea; executing inflated back-to-back agreements with a Hong Kong, Singapore, or other intermediate entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization under the substance-over-form principle; disallowance of the related-party deductions; additional corporate income tax and Local Income Tax surcharge at the recharacterized bracket; negligence surcharge up to 20% of the restored taxable income; potential criminal prosecution where intentional evasion is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who engineered or approved the artificial structure may be held jointly liable for the corporation's unpaid taxes under the corporate-veil-piercing doctrine; senior management can face criminal penalties, asset seizure, and court-ordered restitution; overseas travel may be restricted during active tax criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Unreported Cross-Border Wire Movement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving retainer and crisis-communication fees through personal or offshore accounts outside the Korean banking system, structuring wire receipts to avoid foreign-exchange reporting thresholds, or repatriating dividends and profits without filing required Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines and penalties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, including monetary penalties scaled to the unreported amount; criminal liability under the Financial Transactions Reports Act for failing to report suspicious transactions, punishable by imprisonment up to five years or a fine up to KRW 50 million; tax assessments on undisclosed foreign-source and repatriated income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be prosecuted for knowingly assisting in money-laundering transactions or permitting deficient AML controls; personal fines, forfeiture orders, imprisonment, and travel bans can result; the regulator may separately seek disqualification from holding directorship positions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing the KRW 5 billion Local File threshold filing deadline, failing to prepare contemporaneous master and local documentation, using an unjustified management-fee markup for the overseas PR agency, refusing to provide the NTS with foreign related-party invoices, or obstructing a transfer pricing audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Negligence surcharge of 10% or 20% of the unreported international transaction amount; unilateral transfer pricing adjustment by the NTS; imposition of a 20% additional tax on understated taxable income plus 0.022% daily late-payment interest; intentional or reckless behavior may trigger criminal fines under tax penalty provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing documents or direct the suppression of related-party transaction records may face personal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act; where the company is insolvent, the NTS may pursue a director as the actual taxpayer or secondary taxpayer; travel bans and criminal imprisonment are available for severe intentional noncompliance.
